title: Getting Started With Agent Testing: Why Are Evaluations Important? (Part 1)

chapters.title: Why AI testing differs from traditional testing

features.name: AI evaluations framework
features.description: A comprehensive approach to testing AI features that accounts for non-deterministic behavior, variable inputs, and subjective quality metrics rather than simple pass-fail assertions.
caveats: Quality is subjective and requires metrics

features.name: Programmatic evaluation with data-driven testing via YAML
features.description: A deterministic approach to AI testing that uses YAML to define data-driven test cases with variations in input and bias handling, enabling repeatable evaluation of AI features.

features.name: LLM-based output evaluation
features.description: Using language models to automatically judge and score AI-generated outputs such as emails, product descriptions, or project descriptions against specified criteria.
caveats: Works best for generated text and communication

features.name: Agent benchmarking and observability
features.description: Advanced evaluation scenarios for comparing multiple agents across specific setups, observing metrics like latency, cost, and error rates.
caveats: Not covered in detail in this session

quotes.text: the important part is not necessarily how good your prompt is or your instructions, but how good your evaluations are
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the core thesis that evaluation quality, not prompt engineering, is the key to AI success.

quotes.text: AI is different in that AI has non-deterministic behavior. The uh the inputs will vary.
quotes.why_it_matters: Defines why traditional deterministic testing approaches do not work for AI systems.

quotes.text: the behavior isn't repeatable, and the quality is subjective, and the metrics actually matter more than just a pass-fail
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the fundamental differences in how AI features must be evaluated compared to traditional software.

quotes.text: you need to program the tests in a deterministic way. You can have variation in the input.
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the solution approach of creating deterministic test frameworks that accommodate input variation.

quotes.text: building it in AI AIL and using um data-driven via YAML gives you a framework for basically testing in a deterministic way
quotes.why_it_matters: Specifies the technical tools and approach for implementing repeatable AI testing.

quotes.text: you can use LLMs to try to judge, okay, I asked for this, does the answer reflect what I asked for?
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows how LLMs themselves can be used as validators for subjective output quality.

disclaimers.text: But we're not really going to cover that today. The main focus is on the on the second part.
